Full definitions for 2 tool(s).

build
Compile a Release into its rendered artifacts — returned in memory by default, and also written to `dist/` at the workspace root, where `aggrega build` writes them, when sent `write`. Without `write` the render writes no artifact to disk. Pass the Release path as `release` (absolute, or relative to the workspace). The tool runs the full compiler pipeline through the provider render step and returns the produced files by output-relative path. Use it to see exactly what a Release would emit before writing it, or to inspect one component's rendered output while authoring. In the detailed response format each file's rendered content is included; the concise format returns just the file paths. Sent `write`, the finished render is written through the same write `aggrega build` performs, and the answer names that directory as `output_dir` and lists the files written relative to it; that writes inside the workspace, so over HTTP it needs aggrega:workspace-write. A render failure comes back as actionable guidance rather than a partial write (route it through explain-error if needed): a refusal the compiler raises while compiling the Release reads in the compiler's words with every cause, and travels as a structured `refusal` entry naming the document it points at, the key there and that key's position, with each finding listed under `findings` where it joins several. `auto_pull` resolves the Release's dependencies into the lockfile first, which reaches a registry and writes.

This writes inside the workspace, so over HTTP it needs aggrega:workspace-write. Default false: the artifacts are returned in memory and nothing is written."}},"required":["release"]}

pull
Resolve a Release's catalog and source dependencies into the local cache and write its lockfile — it changes your workspace and reaches the network. Pass the Release path as `release`. By default it reconciles: a recorded pin is honoured and fetched at that version, an unpinned reference is resolved fresh, a reference no longer reached is pruned, and an unchanged dependency set rewrites nothing. Call it when a build reports a drifted lockfile, or declines an external reference the lockfile does not pin — a build renders only from pins the workspace already carries, and this is what makes them exist. Pass `verify` to compare the recorded lockfile against the resolution that reconcile would perform now, honouring the same pins, without writing the lockfile, the plugin trust record or any entity.lock — which is how you detect drift. Pass `upgrade_targets` with entity URIs to re-resolve only those, holding every other pin; no argument re-resolves everything at once, because that discards the whole lockfile and a tool call has nobody to confirm it. A Recipe or FeatureRecipe the Release builds from a catalog directory must have its inputs' pins recorded in the entity.lock beside it, and by default a resolution over one whose lock does not refuses and names the pin tool; pass `pin_sources` to run that same step here instead.

capabilities.name: build
capabilities.description: Compile a Release into its rendered artifacts — returned in memory by default, and also written to `dist/` at the workspace root, where `aggrega build` writes them, when sent `write`. Without `write` the render writes no artifact to disk. Pass the Release path as `release` (absolute, or relative to the workspace). The tool runs the full compiler pipeline through the provider render step and returns the produced files by output-relative path. Use it to see exactly what a Release would emit before writing it, or to inspect one component's rendered output while authoring. In the detailed response format each file's rendered content is included; the concise format returns just the file paths. Sent `write`, the finished render is written through the same write `aggrega build` performs, and the answer names that directory as `output_dir` and lists the files written relative to it; that writes inside the workspace, so over HTTP it needs aggrega:workspace-write. A render failure comes back as actionable guidance rather than a partial write (route it through explain-error if needed): a refusal the compiler raises while compiling the Release reads in the compiler's words with every cause, and travels as a structured `refusal` entry naming the document it points at, the key there and that key's position, with each finding listed under `findings` where it joins several. `auto_pull` resolves the Release's dependencies into the lockfile first, which reaches a registry and writes.

release.description: Path to the Release YAML to build, absolute or relative to the workspace root.

response_format.description: detailed returns each rendered file's content; concise returns only the file paths. Defaults to detailed.

auto_pull.description: Resolve the Release's dependencies into the lockfile before rendering. Reaches a registry and writes the lockfile. Defaults to false. The workspace auto_pull setting turns the same step on for every build, and this adds to it rather than overriding it.

write.description: Write the rendered artifacts to dist/ at the workspace root, where aggrega build writes them, and name that directory and the files written in the answer. This writes inside the workspace, so over HTTP it needs aggrega:workspace-write. Default false: the artifacts are returned in memory and nothing is written.

capabilities.name: pull
capabilities.description: Resolve a Release's catalog and source dependencies into the local cache and write its lockfile — it changes your workspace and reaches the network. Pass the Release path as `release`. By default it reconciles: a recorded pin is honoured and fetched at that version, an unpinned reference is resolved fresh, a reference no longer reached is pruned, and an unchanged dependency set rewrites nothing. Call it when a build reports a drifted lockfile, or declines an external reference the lockfile does not pin — a build renders only from pins the workspace already carries, and this is what makes them exist. Pass `verify` to compare the recorded lockfile against the resolution that reconcile would perform now, honouring the same pins, without writing the lockfile, the plugin trust record or any entity.lock — which is how you detect drift. Pass `upgrade_targets` with entity URIs to re-resolve only those, holding every other pin; no argument re-resolves everything at once, because that discards the whole lockfile and a tool call has nobody to confirm it. A Recipe or FeatureRecipe the Release builds from a catalog directory must have its inputs' pins recorded in the entity.lock beside it, and by default a resolution over one whose lock does not refuses and names the pin tool; pass `pin_sources` to run that same step here instead.

release.description: Path to the Release YAML whose dependencies to resolve, absolute or relative to the workspace root.

verify.description: Compare the recorded lockfile against the resolution a reconcile would perform now, honouring the pins it records, without writing the lockfile, any entity.lock or the plugin trust record. Drift — a pin, or a signature the lockfile or the plugin trust record records that a reconcile would record, replace or clear — and a missing lockfile, are failures. Under the offline posture a recorded signature only its registry can confirm is not checked, and the diagnostics name each one. Cannot be combined with upgrade_targets or pin_sources.

upgrade_targets.description: Entity URIs to re-resolve, in the bare authored form (core/database, for example). Each named pin is dropped and re-resolved to the highest available version; all other pins and the recorded external inputs are held. Omit to reconcile instead. Cannot be combined with verify.

pin_sources.description: Run the entity author's pin step over the Recipes and FeatureRecipes the Release builds from a catalog directory, writing the entity.lock beside each, instead of refusing on one whose lock does not record its pins. Absent follows the workspace's pin_sources_at_pull setting; either value overrides it. Cannot be combined with verify, whichever value it carries.
